summary: National Registry certified paramedic with nearly a decade of continuous full-time prehospital experience across busy 911 and interfacility transport systems. Recognized for strong clinical assessment, calm direction of high-acuity scenes, and consistent documentation and equipment readiness.

experience.title: Paramedic, Field Training Officer
experience.employer: an industry-leading metropolitan emergency medical services organization
bullets: Provide advanced life support assessment and treatment for a 911 response area averaging 12-15 calls per 12-hour shift, covering cardiac, trauma, respiratory, and behavioral emergencies.
Direct scene operations as lead paramedic, delegating tasks to EMT partners and first responders during multi-patient incidents.
Serve as a field training officer for 6-8 new paramedics and EMTs per year, verifying competency in airway management, IV/IO access, 12-lead ECG interpretation, and medication administration.
Maintain 100% compliance with controlled-substance, equipment checkout, and patient care report documentation audits.
Coordinate with receiving emergency departments and specialty care centers to transmit ECGs and pre-arrival reports that reduce handoff time.

experience.title: Paramedic
bullets: Delivered paramedic-level care on interfacility and 911 transports, managing ventilators, vasoactive infusions, and post-surgical patients during transfer.
Performed patient assessments, vital sign monitoring, cardiac rhythm interpretation, and medication administration within protocol and medical direction.
Operated and maintained advanced life support equipment, including defibrillators, infusion pumps, and oxygen delivery systems, with zero unresolved equipment failures.
Completed thorough electronic patient care reports and verbal handoffs for an average of 1,200 transports annually.
Supported mass-gathering standby coverage and surge response alongside local public safety agencies.

experience.title: EMT
experience.employer: a community ambulance and rescue agency
bullets: Responded to emergency and non-emergency calls as part of a two-person crew, performing basic life support, vital signs, bleeding control, splinting, and oxygen therapy.
Assisted paramedic partners with airway adjuncts, CPR, stair-chair and stretcher movement, and scene safety at residences and public venues.
Documented patient encounters and insurance information accurately in electronic records.
Inspected and restocked ambulances at the start of each shift, maintaining readiness of oxygen, suction, and trauma supplies.
Recognized time-critical conditions such as stroke and cardiac arrest and initiated immediate transport and CPR.

skills: Scene safety and incident command support
